newsitem.title: POLAND: Open-air bazaars have 10 pct of Polish exports.
newsitem.headline: Open-air bazaars have 10 pct of Polish exports.

text.p: Poland's bustling open-air bazaars, which have popped up accross the country over the past five years, will account for about 10 percent of the country's total exports this year, a survey by an independent think-tank showed.

"Unregistered exports from bazaars will likely reach some five billion zlotys this year, or 10 percent of total registered exports," Janusz Dabrowski, deputy head of the Gdansk Institute for Market Economy Research (IBnGR), told a news conference.

That compares with total unregistered cross-border exports of $6 billion in 1996 and $6.5 billion next year after some $5 billion worth of goods were taken abroad by cross-border shoppers last year, he said.

In a first study summing up the country's open air markets, IBnGR said total turnover in 1996 from bazaars would likely top seven billion zlotys, equivilent to about two-thirds of this year's planned government budget deficit.
"In 1995, about 60 percent of the cross-border trade went to the West, mainly Germany, and 40 percent to the East...but this year, the ratio could be 50-50," Dabrowski said.
He said cros-border trade across Poland's southern border with Slovakia and the Czech Republic accounted only for one or two percent of all unregistered exports.
Dabrowski said bazaars made up 40 percent of retail space in Poland, while the biggest 15 market-places alone employed 130,000 people and served 220,000 costumers per day.
